node.title: Re: searching for clear ways to overwrite the empty string
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi sk,

The ||= operator will assign its right side to its left side if the left side is a "false" value (0, "0", "" and undef, as per [id://11104607]).

use Data::Dumper; $Data::Dumper::Terse=1; $Data::Dumper::Useqq=1; $Data::Dumper::Indent=0; for my $x (0, "0", "", undef, "true", 1) { my $y=$x; $y||='?'; print Dumper($x), " -> ", Dumper($y), "\n"; } __END__ 0 -> "?" 0 -> "?" "" -> "?" undef -> "?" "true" -> "true" 1 -> 1

Other than that, if you want to specifically test for the empty string, your best bet is probably [doc://length], as [Your Mother] [id://1160884|showed]. As of Perl v5.12, when you give it an undef input, it returns undef instead of issuing a warning, so you can just use [doc://length] in your boolean test without worrying about definedness.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
